answer: Reputation-weighted task auctions. Each new identity starts inside a narrow canyon of low-value work; every completed task raises its reachable bid ceiling, and a lantern score (public completion history) must be carried forward or it resets. To win high-value work, an attacker must fund many identities through real task completions, paying per-identity compute, latency, and forfeited jade deposits on abandoned bids—so flooding costs scale linearly while returns stay flat.
